Nina: Quick flag 3 — new reranker bring-up (int8) shows NDCG flat but MRR@10 down ~6.5% on our canonical holdout.
Omar: raw?
Nina: float MRR@10=0.513 -> int8 MRR@10=0.480; NDCG@10 float=0.712 -> int8=0.713. harness run id run/2026-05-04/22
Priya: interesting. Could be dataset sampling differences or candidate pooling order change. MRR is sensitive to top-1 swaps.
Nina: I dug in and found the candidate curation step sometimes de-duplicates by URL fingerprint now, which reorders the candidate list for some queries. Example diff: 
```
q: "reset password"
before pool: [kb-reset, community-reset, vendor-reset]
after pool : [community-reset, kb-reset, vendor-reset]
```
Nina: small reorder like that can flip the top result under quant noise.
Omar: did we also change PTQ config? per_channel or calib samples?
Nina: PTQ: int8_static, per_channel=false, calib=4096, seed=13
Priya: two-track repro: A) revert pool dedupe order, B) switch PTQ to per_channel=true + more calib samples. Run A/B on a 8k holdout.
Nina: pushed bench diff and tiny repro script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/821
eval-bot: shadowbench queued sb-821 (8k) est 90m
Priya: local 2k probe results: revert-order restores MRR from .480 -> .507, per_channel alone -> .495, both -> .510 (slightly better than float). So biggest effect is candidate ordering.
Omar: action items: 1) Make candidate curation deterministic (stable sort) + document ordering guarantees for downstream evals, 2) default per_channel PTQ for rerankers, 3) add a tiny unit test that permutes candidate pools but asserts no >2% MRR variance in rerank-smoke.
Nina: opened PR #821 with stable sort + bench regen. Will follow up on PTQ default change.
eval-bot: sb-821 complete: patched vs baseline -> NDCG@10 +0.05%, MRR@10 +4.8% (patched wins)
Priya: recommend merge after perf sign-off and add a note in onboarding doc about candidate pool determinism.
Nina: thanks all, closing unless someone sees edgecases.
